title: The chosen family
hookLine: Allah chose Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim and the family of Imran (3:33)

lines: A PAGE IN THE FRONT OF AN OLD BOOK.
cards: Some families keep a list: a page in the front of an old book, a chart an aunt made, a grandparent who can recite the names back five generations and gets annoyed when you lose track.
Al 'Imran is named after a family, and in verse thirty-three it gives its own short list. Four names.
Not a family tree in the usual sense: a list of who was chosen, and the doorway to the stories this surah is about to tell.

teach.b: Pickthall translates 3:33: "Lo! Allah preferred Adam and Noah and the Family of Abraham and the Family of 'Imran above (all His) creatures." Adam, where the human story begins, as the Qur'an tells it.
Nuh, Noah, who carried the survivors through the flood. The family of Ibrahim, running through Isma'il and Ishaq to a long line of prophets, and, Muslims believe, to Muhammad ﷺ.
And the family of Imran. Who is Imran? The Qur'an calls Maryam, the mother of Isa, the daughter of Imran, and many commentators take this to be her father.
Others connected the name to Amram, the father of Musa and Harun. The verse doesn't say, and both views appear in the classical books.
The verb is istafa, from a root meaning purity, the clear, best part of something. The Prophet's title al-Mustafa, the chosen one, comes from the same root.

teach.h: A WEIGHT PASSED HAND TO HAND
teach.b: Then 3:34, in Pickthall's words: "They were descendants one of another." One line, linked from Adam onward.
But chosen doesn't mean easy, and the surah shows it right away: Imran's wife, pregnant, promises her unborn child to God, and is surprised when the child is a girl.
That girl is Maryam. Over the next days come Zakariyya, who looked after her, and the angels who spoke to her. Being chosen, in these stories, isn't a badge.
It's a weight passed hand to hand, and each person in the line had to carry it in their own hard moment.

how: Muslims honor the prophets named in 3:33 and their families, and the story of the family of Imran, Maryam's family, is told at length in the surah that bears its name.

games.q: you're Imran's wife. you've promised your unborn child to serve God. the child is born, and it's a girl. what does the story say?
o: she names her Maryam and asks God to protect her.
she gives the child to her sister.
games.why: she names her Maryam and seeks God's protection for her and her offspring (3:36). she keeps the promise, and the girl is accepted.

practice: Think back along your own line: a parent, a grandparent, someone further back whose name you only half know, or, if family is complicated, whoever raised you, taught you or held you up, because a line doesn't have to be only blood.
Pick one person and name one thing they passed to you, a habit, a phrase, a way of standing. If you pray, you can thank God for them, in whatever words are yours.

wordCard.voice: Istafa, chose, the purest part of something. Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim and the family of Imran, chosen, and descendants one of another. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: chose, picked the purest (3:33); the same root gives al-Mustafa, a title of the Prophet.

carryVoice: Your line: a chosen line. What was handed to you is part of yours. Until tomorrow.
